prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1186; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a sideswipe that occurred while the other driver was changing lanes. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Photos taken at the scene show damage consistent with the described impact, and the repair estimate reflects the same panels. Police records and the statements of people at the scene confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time. No independent witnesses have come forward to add to the account.

Entry 3: The claimant's neck strain is consistent in type and severity with the force of a side impact of this kind. No prior injury to the same body area appears in the records we have reviewed. The driver is named on the policy, and nothing in the file suggests the vehicle was damaged before coverage began.

Entry 4: Treatment has followed a typical course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits that became less frequent as the claimant's condition improved. The claimant has given the same account of the collision in each conversation so far, including through counsel.

Entry 5: No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection notes. The repair scope matches the photographs and the reported point of contact on the vehicle.

Entry 6: File reviewed and details checked against the photos, police report, and medical records. Findings so far are consistent across sources, and the claim will proceed to settlement review with counsel's correspondence on file.
